page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The F64als_v7 achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, alongside high memory bandwidth scores, reaching 410.03 GB/sec for large-block read operations. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform efficiently, as evidenced by top-tier results in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Database and key-value store performance is also notable, with Redis SET operations reaching 171.03 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the F64als_v7 is its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the lack of local storage, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive local caching. However, for compute-heavy workloads, the dedicated high-frequency AMD cores offer strong qualitative cost efficiency by maximizing raw processing throughput per resource unit. It is highly suited for batch processing, web serving, CPU-based machine learning inference, and computational engineering tasks.
